correctness.rationale: An acyclic orientation determines a unique word of colors: linear extensions differ by swaps of incomparable vertices, and distinct colors are adjacent in the graph and comparable in the orientation. The consecutive monochromatic blocks give the cover relations: any two vertices in consecutive blocks are joined by an edge with no intervening vertex on a directed path; vertices in more distant blocks are related by paths through intermediate blocks. The cover graph is connected. Writing s_j for block sizes, its edge surplus over n−1 is sum over interior j of (s_j−1) plus sum over consecutive pairs of (s_j−1)(s_{j+1}−1), proving the stated tree cases including two blocks. A non-tree is nonsimplicial by its facet count; a tree's signed root normals form a lattice basis by leaf deletion, so the dual normal cone is smooth in any characteristic. For r≥3 the all-color projection removes the two-block term. Ordered labeled blocks contribute e^{x_i}−1, with x_i for singleton interiors; the two displayed resolvents sum exactly these transitions, with coefficient multiplied by the product of the class factorials. Independently enumerating all orientations and computing transitive closure and cover edges, without classifying by blocks, gave (smooth,total)=(58,78),(288,426),(1240,2286) in the three stated examples.
residual_risks: Checks concern the normal fan, not the face fan or a toric edge embedding. Finite counts do not establish the all-parameter statement; the block argument does.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad tree theorem by itself does not count smooth vertices, but the prior explicit ordered-partition preposet for this exact multipartite family makes the restriction local between consecutive blocks.

evidence: Chapoton–Pilaud's ordered-partition preposet deletes exactly the within-block relations for a vertex; therefore the Hasse edges are the complete bipartite graphs between successive blocks. PRW then tests the tree condition. An interior block of size ≥2 and one chosen vertex from each neighbor produce a four-cycle; singleton interiors produce the tree immediately. The tree incidence basis gives integral regularity without an additional classification.

In the prior count for an allowed color word let m_i be the number of interior i positions and e_i the number of endpoint i positions. To enforce singleton interiors, select labels for those m_i ordered positions, then map the remaining labels surjectively onto the e_i labeled endpoint positions. The factor is (a_i)_{m_i} Surj(a_i−m_i,e_i), with zero for a_i<m_i. Its EGF is x_i^{m_i}(e^{x_i}−1)^{e_i}. Summing the same allowed words by the standard adjacency matrix yields the displayed smooth series. For r≥3 the separate two-position term vanishes identically after all-color projection.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is an explicit short specialization of the previously established block model and local cone theorem and a routine restriction of the prior labeled word enumeration, not an independent gap that survives mechanical implication. The cited overlap is older primary mathematics, regardless of the later catalogue dates.

originality.rationale: The mathematics is correct, but the strongest earlier sources supply both the exact multipartite block-poset model and the general tree/facet criterion. They mechanically give the singleton-interior rule, and the smooth series is the ordinary word-count transfer formula with interior block weights restricted to the degree-one term. The unrefined count is explicitly covered by prior work. No earlier literal printing of the refined matrix expression was found; the failure is for mechanical implication, not a claim of verbatim prior publication. The substantial later catalogue overlap is not used to infer earlier priority.
residual_risks: No earlier literal statement of the exact refined matrix series verified. No pre-October-18 source was established for the frozen record's assertion about an earlier explicitly enumerated two-color smooth specialization. Neither point affects the demonstration of mechanical implication from earlier general and multipartite results.

value.rationale: Smooth fixed points form a natural invariant and the transfer formula is a convenient exposition, but the purported new refinement applies the existing tree criterion to the existing exact block model and changes only the allowed weights of the interior positions. Under the stated standard this routine restriction, already mechanically implied without a new classification or enumeration step, does not establish an independently useful unresolved fact; the illustrative small exact values are coefficients of the same restriction. No genuine surviving valuable remainder in the assigned claim was found to repair.
residual_risks: This judgment is specific to the submitted fixed-point result, not to finer strata, adjacency, or other questions about these normal fans.
